speaker: Doctor
text: I see you've already provided your history; could you describe the specific appearance of your skin lesions, including their color, shape, and any changes you've noticed over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history; the combination of non-healing, crusty lesions on the penis and finger in a 62-year-old smoker raises significant concern for squamous cell carcinoma. Have you noticed any bleeding, pain, or rapid growth in these areas, and do you recall any recent sun exposure to your hand?

text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (Penile and Dorsal Hand)
